title: Divorce and Mercy

questions.question: Under what condition can a man divorce his wife?
options: If he finds some indecency in her
If he is tired of her
questions.correctAnswer: If he finds some indecency in her
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:1 (ESV): "...if then she finds no favor in his eyes because he has found some indecency in her..."

questions.question: Can a man remarry his divorced wife after she has married another and been divorced/widowed?
options: No, that would be an abomination
questions.correctAnswer: No, that would be an abomination
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:4 (ESV): "then her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife..."

questions.question: What is the privilege of a newly married man?
options: He shall not go out with the army or be charged with any business for one year
questions.correctAnswer: He shall not go out with the army or be charged with any business for one year
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:5 (ESV): "When a man is newly married, he shall not go out with the army... He shall be free at home one year..."

questions.question: What should not be taken as a pledge (security for loan)?
options: A mill or an upper millstone
questions.correctAnswer: A mill or an upper millstone
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:6 (ESV): "No one shall take a mill or an upper millstone in pledge, for that would be taking a life in pledge."

questions.question: What happens to a kidnapper (steals one of his brothers)?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:7 (ESV): "If a man is found stealing one of his brothers... that thief shall die."

questions.question: Who should be remembered regarding leprosy?
options: Miriam (what the Lord did to her)
questions.correctAnswer: Miriam (what the Lord did to her)
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:9 (ESV): "Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam on the way..."

questions.question: What is the rule about entering a neighbor's house to take a pledge?
options: You shall stand outside; the man shall bring it out to you
You can take what you want
questions.correctAnswer: You shall stand outside; the man shall bring it out to you
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:10–11 (ESV): "...You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you make the loan shall bring the pledge out to you."

questions.question: If the pledge is a poor man's cloak, when must it be returned?
options: At sunset, so he may sleep in it
questions.correctAnswer: At sunset, so he may sleep in it
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:13 (ESV): "You shall restore to him the pledge as the sun sets, that he may sleep in his cloak and bless you."

questions.question: How often should a hired servant be paid?
options: Each day before the sun goes down
questions.correctAnswer: Each day before the sun goes down
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:15 (ESV): "You shall give him his wages on the same day, before the sun sets..."

questions.question: Who should not be put to death for the children?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:16 (ESV): "Fathers shall not be put to death because of their children, nor shall children be put to death because of their fathers."

questions.question: Whose garment should not be taken in pledge?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:17 (ESV): "You shall not... take a widow's garment in pledge."

questions.question: If you forget a sheaf in the field, should you go back to get it?
options: No, it shall be for the sojourner, the fatherless, and the widow
questions.correctAnswer: No, it shall be for the sojourner, the fatherless, and the widow
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:19 (ESV): "When you reap your harvest... and have forgotten a sheaf in the field, you shall not go back to get it..."

questions.question: What is the similar rule for olive trees and vineyards?
options: Do not go over the boughs again or strip them bare; leave for the poor
questions.correctAnswer: Do not go over the boughs again or strip them bare; leave for the poor
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:20–21 (ESV): "When you beat your olive trees, you shall not go over them again... When you gather the grapes... you shall not strip it afterward..."

questions.question: Why are these charity laws given (remembering what)?
options: You were a slave in the land of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: You were a slave in the land of Egypt
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:22 (ESV): "You shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt; therefore I command you to do this."

questions.question: Each person shall be put to death for whose sin?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 24:16 (ESV): "Each one shall be put to death for his own sin."

key_verse_text: Fathers shall not be put to death because of their children, nor shall children be put to death because of their fathers. Each one shall be put to death for his own sin. (ESV)
